title: Cover GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS on the integrity security axis (BEFORE/AFTER/RACE arms)
description:
FILED BY worker-b8af1a87 from task-e3d5fd057ca24d50a973cb61e4911f5f, which DECLARED the boundary and disclosed this red rather than hiding it. QA's reject on that task said explicitly: "Do NOT delete the roster entry to quiet (3); that hides a real boundary" and "file the follow-up for the 3 arms. Keep the entry."

MEASURED RED, verbatim, reproduced at HEAD by `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts` (run it directly: `pnpm test:security` dies earlier on a FOREIGN TS6133 before vitest starts):

  FAIL  integrity-boundaries.security.ts > integrity axis versus the declared-boundary roster > reads a positive number of integrity entries off the roster
  AssertionError: expected [ ...(14) ] to have a length of 13 but got 14
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106:30

  FAIL  ... > covers every integrity boundary the roster declares (roster minus covered is empty)
  AssertionError: expected [ 'GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS' ] to deeply equal []
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:111:75

  FAIL  ... > generates a positive, three-armed case count for GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS
  AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:124:27

  Test Files  1 failed | 8 passed (9) / Tests  3 failed | 476 passed (479)

CAUSE, stated plainly: task-e3d5fd05 added the roster entry `{ constant: "GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS", file: "packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-issues.ts", axis: "integrity" }` at tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:199. Rostering a boundary ACTIVATES a closed coverage ratchet in the axis slice: integrity-boundaries.security.ts parses the roster's committed bytes for its own axis tag and demands BEFORE, AFTER and RACE hostile arms per constant. There is no quiet tag — retagging to `scheduler-activation` was measured and moves the same three failures to that slice.

WORK: add BEFORE/AFTER/RACE hostile arms for GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS in the integrity axis's hostile-cases module, following the shape the sibling arms already use (each forgery arm RE-SEALS through production and carries an `integrity` thunk asserted ok:true first), and bump the pinned integrity cardinality 13 -> 14 at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106 plus EXPECTED_ROSTER_SIZE / EXPECTED_DISTRIBUTION in the roster if they also moved.

SUBJECT UNDER TEST, already landed and green: packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-issues.ts (GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS = GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC | GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY | GRAPH_VALIDATION), the codec in graph-content.ts / graph-content-fields.ts / graph-content-format.ts, and `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` = Test Files 45 passed / Tests 1411 passed.

DO NOT close this by deleting the roster entry.
definitionOfDone: tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts reports GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS as covered: roster-minus-covered is empty and armsFor("GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS") contains BEFORE, AFTER and RACE with a nonzero asserted case count.
The pinned integrity roster cardinality is corrected to the true count (13 -> 14) and any sibling cardinality assertion that moved with it, with no roster entry deleted or retagged to a quieter axis.

Each new hostile arm re-seals through the production codec (encodeGraphContent / decodeGraphContent) rather than a test-local reimplementation, and asserts the exact GRAPH_CONTENT_* code and layer it expects, never merely that the operation failed.
`npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts` exits 0 with a nonzero Test Files count line, and a mutation drill on one new arm makes a NAMED test go red on its own assertion.
taskRails: Never delete or retag the GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS roster entry to quiet the gate - the boundary is real and removing it hides it.
Owned paths are the tests/security integrity-axis files only; do not edit packages/scheduler production sources, which are green and owned elsewhere.

implementationPlan.description: Reproduce the baseline and record TWO corrections to the task text, both measured by the architect on 2026-08-17. Read-only. Run `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts` and confirm EXACTLY three failures: the cardinality assertion at :106 (expected 14 to have length 13), the roster-minus-covered assertion at :111 (['GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS'] vs []), and the three-armed count at :124 (expected 0 to be greater than 0). CORRECTION 1 -- THE TASK RAIL IS STALE: rail 3 says `pnpm test:security` dies on a FOREIGN TS6133 before vitest starts and tells you to work around it. `npx tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json --noEmit` now EXITS 0; that foreign red has CLEARED since the task was filed. Re-run it yourself to confirm, then use the full `pnpm test:security` as your gate and say in the note that the workaround was no longer needed. A baseline foreign red can clear mid-task, and carrying a stale workaround hides the real gate. CORRECTION 2 -- THE ROSTER HALF IS ALREADY DONE: the task says to bump EXPECTED_ROSTER_SIZE / EXPECTED_DISTRIBUTION "if they also moved". They already moved. tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:226 reads `EXPECTED_ROSTER_SIZE = 92` and the distribution at :233 already credits `packages/scheduler: 8`, with the entry at :199 and its provenance comment at :104 and :216. So the ONLY cardinality edit left is `toHaveLength(13)` -> `toHaveLength(14)` at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106. Do not touch boundary-roster.security.ts, and above all do not delete or retag the roster entry -- QA's reject on task-e3d5fd05 said so explicitly and the boundary is real.

Study the template before writing an arm, because the shape is load-bearing and the file already answers every question. Read tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts:265-297 -- `codecCases` for PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_LAYERS is the exact model: one `before`, one `after`, one `racing`, each naming the constant, each carrying an explicit `{code, layer}` expectation built with `layerOf(CONSTANT, "MEMBER")`, and each with a comment explaining WHY that layer is provably the branch that answered. Note the four helpers at :170-187: `before` (BEFORE arm), `after` (AFTER arm), `forged` (AFTER arm PLUS an `integrity` thunk), and `racing` (RACE arm, run through `probeRacing(RACE_BOUND, left, right)`). USE `forged`, NOT `after`, FOR THE DIGEST ARM: integrity-boundaries.security.ts has a separate assertion that re-seals at least one forgery per digest-bearing boundary by filtering `entry.arm !== "RACE" && entry.integrity !== undefined`, so a plain `after` would satisfy the three-arm count and still leave GRAPH_CONTENT uncovered by the reseal check. Finally note the assembly at :1204 -- `INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES` spreads thirteen named arrays; you will add a fourteenth and must spread it there or the cases exist and are never collected.

Write the three arms in tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts as a new `graphContentCases` array, following `codecCases` in structure and comment discipline. The subject is landed and green: `encodeGraphContent` / `decodeGraphContent` from the bare `@moe/scheduler` root -- go through the published codec, never `canonicalGraphJson` or the raw hash, which are deliberately withheld so no consumer can mint bytes the kernel never accepted. `GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS` has three members (GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, GRAPH_VALIDATION) and `GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES` offers DIGEST_MISMATCH, MALFORMED, NONCANONICAL, NOT_BYTES, TOO_LARGE, UNREADABLE and UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA. Suggested shape, and PREFER SPREADING THE THREE LAYER MEMBERS ACROSS THE THREE ARMS so the whole constant is exercised rather than one member three times: BEFORE -- bytes that never become content (truncated or not-bytes) refusing at GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, where nothing later on the path is reachable; FORGED/AFTER -- encode a valid content, then carry its digest onto a different content so shape and canonicalisation both pass and ONLY the re-derived digest comparison can refuse, at GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, with the `integrity` thunk re-sealing through production and asserted ok:true first; RACE -- a re-spelled canonical encoding raced against a non-canonical or duplicate-key variant. Assert the exact code AND layer on every arm, never merely that the call failed. Then spread `graphContentCases` into `INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES` at :1204.

Bump the one stale pin: `expect(ROSTER_INTEGRITY).toHaveLength(13)` -> `14` at tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106. Change nothing else in that file -- the roster-minus-covered assertion at :111, the covered-minus-roster assertion at :117, the three-armed `it.each` at :121-131 and the reseal assertion below it must all start passing because the ARMS now exist, not because an assertion was loosened. If any of them still fails after step 3, the arms are wrong; fix the arms, never the assertion. Leave the sibling `it("reads a positive number of integrity entries off the roster")` guard intact: its `toBeGreaterThan(0)` is what stops a silently-zero roster parse from making every set assertion below pass vacuously.

Mutation drill, then confirm the arms are real rather than merely present. DoD 4 requires a drill on one new arm making a NAMED test go red on its own assertion. Do two, because two different things could be fake: Drill 1 (the expectation is pinned) -- change the expected `code` on the BEFORE arm to a different GRAPH_CONTENT_* member; the named case must go RED on the code comparison, not on a crash and not on a count. Drill 2 (the forgery really re-seals) -- make the `integrity` thunk on the FORGED arm return a value that was not re-sealed through the production codec; the reseal assertion must go RED. If drill 2 stays green, the thunk is not actually exercising production and the arm is decorative. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore exact bytes by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat -- tests/security/` showing 0 added and 0 deleted afterwards. One drill at a time -- a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

Adversarial review, commit, and gate. ATTACKER PASS: does any arm assert only that a call rejected, without pinning code AND layer? Could an EARLIER guard be answering instead of the layer named -- for the BEFORE arm, is it genuinely true that nothing later on the path is reachable, and did you write down why, as the sibling cases do? Does the RACE arm actually interleave through `probeRacing(RACE_BOUND, ...)` rather than running two independent calls? Does any arm reach past the published codec into withheld mechanics? Is `graphContentCases` spread into INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES (cases that exist but are never collected pass every check by being invisible)? Confirm no roster entry was deleted, retagged, or moved to a quieter axis, and that no packages/scheduler production source was touched -- those are green and owned elsewhere. COMMIT: `git status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry with `git restore --staged -- <path>`, commit ONLY tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts and tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts by explicit pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`. GATE, foreground and `&&`-chained so no red leg is masked: `pnpm test:security && pnpm typecheck`. Per step 1 the foreign TS6133 has cleared, so run the real script rather than the vitest workaround; if it has returned, disclose it verbatim and fall back to `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts`. Read the OUTPUT: the run must print a nonzero `Test Files` count line and integrity-boundaries.security.ts must report 0 failures, up from the 3 measured in step 1.

DEFECT: the new RACE arm cannot detect an ADMISSION - the one defect a race arm exists to find.

MY DRILL (restored byte-identical, sha256 031bf0f6..., `git status --porcelain -- tests/security/` empty, HEAD sha == on-disk): I replaced the RACE left leg with `decodeGraphContent(sealedGraphContent("dev-author-a").bytes)` - production's OWN canonical bytes, which the codec ADMITS with `{ok:true}`. Result: `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts` -> EXIT 0, `Tests 63 passed (63)`. GREEN on an admission.

MECHANISM: `soleIssue` (:1237) THROWS when `issues` is not a length-1 array, and an admitted `{ok:true,value}` carries none. probeRacing catches that into `{status:"rejected",reason}`, `legValue` returns the Error, `admitted(Error)` is false. So integrity-boundaries.security.ts:204-205 and the whole-slice invariant at :214 both pass on an admission. The 13 siblings lack this hole: `asLayered` never throws, so an admitted sibling leg lands as `{ok:true}` and reddens.

AGGRAVATING: `GRAPH_CONTENT_NONCANONICAL` occurs in tests/security exactly once - a comment at :1383. Your two race legs are the suite's only probes of a non-canonical spelling, so a codec that began admitting a duplicated `hash` key or a re-spelled envelope reddens nothing.

VERIFIED GOOD: drilling the BEFORE arm's code (UNREADABLE -> MALFORMED) reddens the NAMED test on its own comparison - `refusal code mismatch: expected GRAPH_CONTENT_MALFORMED, observed GRAPH_CONTENT_UNREADABLE`.

FOREIGN, DO NOT FIX: `pnpm test:security` is now exit 1, 4 failures in the boundary-roster and durable-store slices, all `PROVIDER_EFFECT_SETTLEMENT_LAYER@packages/runner/src/supervisor/provider-settlement-contracts.ts` - untracked peer file, landed after your 22:45:50 gate. 483 tests both runs.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The task is well-specified and its measurement reproduced exactly, so the plan mostly supplies the template and two corrections rather than re-deciding anything. REJECTED: (a) deleting or retagging the roster entry -- forbidden by the task rail and by QA's reject on task-e3d5fd05 ("Do NOT delete the roster entry to quiet (3); that hides a real boundary"), and the description records that retagging to scheduler-activation was measured and simply moves the same three failures to that slice; (b) using the plain `after` helper for the digest arm -- it would satisfy the three-armed count while leaving the separate per-digest-bearing-boundary reseal assertion uncovered, so the digest arm must use `forged`, which carries the `integrity` thunk; (c) putting the new arms in a new sibling module -- the axis file already groups thirteen constants into named arrays and the pattern is per-axis, not per-constant, so a fourteenth array in the same file is the consistent choice (the file is 1208 lines, but the epic's line cap binds PRODUCTION sources, not test tables); (d) touching boundary-roster.security.ts -- measured as already correct, see below. Suggested spreading the three GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS members across the three arms rather than exercising one member three times, since the constant is what the roster declares covered.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is an arm that exists without testing anything: the three-armed assertion only counts arms, so a case asserting merely that a call rejected would satisfy the ratchet while pinning nothing. Every arm must assert code AND layer, and drill 1 exists to prove the code is pinned. Second risk is the digest arm using `after` instead of `forged` -- it would pass the count and silently leave the reseal assertion uncovered for a digest-bearing boundary; drill 2 targets exactly that, and a green drill 2 means the integrity thunk is not exercising production. Third, an arm can redden for the wrong reason: if an earlier guard answers before the layer you named, the case passes while testing a different branch, which is why the sibling cases each carry a written justification for why their layer is reachable -- copy that discipline. Fourth, cases that are written but never spread into INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES are invisible and every check still passes; verify the spread at :1204. Fifth, do not fix a still-failing ratchet assertion by loosening it -- only :106 may change, and only 13 -> 14. Sixth, the foreign typecheck red has cleared but could return; disclose it verbatim rather than working around it silently. Seventh, this task owns tests/security integrity-axis files ONLY -- packages/scheduler sources are green and owned elsewhere, and boundary-roster.security.ts is already correct. Finally, never delete or retag the roster entry: retagging was already measured to move the same three failures to another slice, and QA rejected that approach by name on the parent task.

Then re-drill and confirm RED.
